name: Japan
headline: Industrial discipline against an aging population.
summary: Japan achieved lightning industrialization after 1945, then endured the bubble and deflation. Its public debt is the highest in the developed world, but it is held by residents and denominated in yen. The real challenge is demographic: fewer workers, more social spending.

history.title: Meiji Restoration
history.text: Japan opens its economy and industrializes under state direction. It copies Western technologies, creates conglomerates (zaibatsu), and builds a modern navy.

history.title: Defeat and rebuilding
history.text: After Hiroshima and Nagasaki, the country is occupied and reformed. It renounces war, adopts a pacifist constitution, and focuses on growth.

history.title: The Japanese miracle
history.text: The Liberal Democratic Party dominates politics. The state coordinates industry and banks fund investment: growth exceeds 8% a year.

history.title: The bubble bursts
history.text: Equities and real estate collapse. Banks accumulate bad loans and the country enters a long deflation.

history.title: Banking crisis
history.text: The failure of major institutions forces the state to recapitalize the system. Public debt explodes to prevent a credit collapse.

history.title: Abenomics
history.text: Three arrows: aggressive monetary policy, fiscal stimulus, and structural reforms. The Bank of Japan buys debt on a massive scale.

history.title: Exit from negative rates
history.text: The BOJ normalizes cautiously. The yen stays weak and the stock market returns to peaks, carried by corporate governance and semiconductors.

institutions.executive: Prime Minister drawn from the Diet; Emperor as a symbol
institutions.legislature: Bicameral Diet: House of Representatives and House of Councillors
institutions.central_bank: Bank of Japan (BOJ), historically highly accommodative
institutions.law: Civil law based on the German model, strong administrative stability
institutions.fact: The BOJ holds a huge share of Japanese public debt, so sustainability depends on its policy.

dependencies.name: United States
dependencies.note: Security and market access, but risk of trade friction.

gdp_growth.note: Growth is weak: consumption suffers from aging and exports depend on the global cycle.

inflation.note: After decades of deflation, inflation is taking hold. Good news for real wages, as long as it stays moderate.

debt_gdp.note: The ratio is extreme, but the debt is in yen and locally held. Sustainability depends on rates and nominal growth.

policy_rate.note: The BOJ exits its ultra-accommodative regime very slowly. Every hike raises the cost of debt and supports the yen.

unemployment.note: Unemployment is very low, but the labor force shrinks. Labor scarcity weighs on small businesses.

reserves.note: Japan holds enormous reserves, mostly in foreign securities. They act as a buffer in any yen stress.

rating.note: The rating stays high thanks to institutional stability and locally held debt, despite the record debt ratio.

cds.note: The market prices no short-term default risk. Japanese CDS are among the lowest in the G7.

equity_index.note: The index benefits from a weak yen, corporate governance, and the semiconductor cycle.

currency.name: Yen
currency.note: A weak yen helps exporters but makes imported energy and household cost of living more expensive.

strengths: Stable institutions and a high standard of living.
A first-class industrial and technological base.
Public debt financed locally and in yen.
risks: Aging and a shrinking labor force.
Record public debt sensitive to higher rates.
Energy and demographic dependence on imports.
opportunities: Semiconductors, robotics, and automation for an aging society.
Improving corporate governance and returning capital to shareholders.

quiz.question: Why is Japanese debt less risky than it looks?
options: It is held by residents and in yen
It is guaranteed by the United States
quiz.explanation: Debt in the national currency, held by residents and a domestic central bank, is easier to refinance. That does not remove the risk, it transforms it.
